sections.heading: Prefixes
sections.body: Prefixes change meaning in predictable ways:

sections.heading: Suffixes that make nouns and adjectives
sections.body:
- *-ción / -sión* (action → noun): *organizar → la organización, decidir → la decisión*
- *-dad / -tad* (quality): *feliz → la felicidad, libre → la libertad*
- *-miento* (process): *crecer → el crecimiento* (growth)
- *-ero / -era* (job, container): *el zapatero* (shoemaker), *la panadería → el panadero*, *la azucarera* (sugar bowl)
- *-able / -ible* (can be done): *comer → comestible* (edible), *lavar → lavable* (washable)
- *-oso / -osa* (full of): *peligro → peligroso* (dangerous), *ruido → ruidoso* (noisy)
- *-mente* (adverb): *fácil → fácilmente*

sections.heading: Diminutives and augmentatives
sections.body:
Diminutives in *-ito / -ita* (and *-cito* after *-e, -n, -r*) express smallness, affection or politeness. In Latin America they are everywhere: *un cafecito, ahorita* (right now, in a moment — Mexico), *un momentito, cerquita* (very close), *despacito* (nice and slow). Other diminutives: *-illo* (*un poquillo*), *-ico* (Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba: *chiquitico*).

Augmentatives in *-ón / -ona, -ote / -ota, -azo* make things bigger or stronger, often pejorative: *una casona* (big house), *un grandote* (big guy), *un golpazo* (a huge blow). *-azo* can also mean "a blow with": *un portazo* (a door slam), *un codazo* (an elbow jab).
